title: [Decision] A record opened as a full page sends its list back to page 1: should the console list keep the page a reader turned to?
body:
Filing gate: ② a decision only the maintainer can make. The maintainer asked for this card directly, in a non-seat Claude Code session (https://claude.ai/code/session_01RKKVngnSz3HSwwHD7UfpjG), and asked that the PM decide whether and how it gets built. ⛔ Not a claim. Suggested-grade: p3 (user-visible, but the default desktop path is not affected).

## Maintainer quick read

A reader on page 2 of a long list opens a record. If the record opens as a **full page**, going back to the list shows **page 1**, and the reader has to page forward again to find their place. If the record opens in the **drawer** (the desktop default), the list stays on page 2. Decide whether the list should come back on the page the reader left, and if so, where that page number is kept.

## What happens today (read from code at `main`, not yet reproduced in a running app)

The list's current page is local component state that starts at 1 and is never written anywhere else:

- `ui/packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx:2226`: `const [serverPage, setServerPage] = React.useState(1);`
- `ui/packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx:7384`: the pager only calls `setServerPage(p)`. The URL does not change.

Whether the page survives depends on whether the list unmounts:

| How the record opens | When | Back on the list |
|---|---|---|
| Drawer (`?recordId=…` over the list) | Desktop default (`navigation.mode` defaults to `drawer`, `useNavigationOverlay.ts:368`; reader preference `drawer`) | **Page 2**: the list stays mounted (`objectViewRecordNavigation.ts:330`) |
| Full page (`:objectName/record/:recordId`) | Object declares `navigation.mode: 'page'`; reader preference `page` (Display menu); "Open as full page" from the drawer | **Page 1**: the record route is a sibling of the list route (`app-shell/src/console/AppContent.tsx:170`), so `ObjectView`/`ListView` unmount and remount with `useState(1)` |
| Phone (≤ 640 px) | Every record opens as a page (`ObjectView.tsx:951-953`, #27058) | **Page 1**: same reason. Only the record page's own scroll is remembered (`useRecordPageScrollMemory`), not the list's page |

Separately, and on purpose, any change to object, filter, sort, search, grouping, page size or view snaps the list back to page 1 (`ListView.tsx:4021-4037`), and a page past the end is clamped to the last reachable one (`ListView.tsx:3903`). Every option below keeps both behaviours.

## Governing text

- `ui/packages/app-shell/src/urlParams.ts:63-65`: "Page-scoped params (`q`, `limit`, `offset`, `view`, `type`, `review`, `package`, …) belong to their page's own contract and are NOT reserved here — but they must not collide with the names above." A list page number in the URL is a page-scoped param under this rule. It must not reuse a reserved name (`recordId`, `form`, `tab`, `related`, …).
- `ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/AppContent.tsx` (docblock above `RECORD_NAMED_PAGE_ROUTE`): "`page` is a page-scoped list parameter elsewhere". This is a reason to check the bare name `page` for collisions before choosing it.
- No ADR rules on list pagination state. Search: `node scripts/pm/check-prior-rulings.mjs --terms pagination,pager,page-number,list-state,back-navigation` → 1 hit (AGENTS.md:820, unrelated: REST pagination helpers).

Protocol: no spec change in any option. `ListViewSchema.pagination` (`pageSize`, `pageSizeOptions`) is untouched. This is console behaviour only.

## Premise (re-check before acting)

- The page is still local state: `grep -n "useState(1)" ui/packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` still shows `serverPage`.
- The record route is still a sibling of the list route: `grep -n "record/:recordId'" ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/AppContent.tsx`.
- Not yet measured in a running app: whether a phone list uses the same server pager or loads more as you scroll. If phone lists load more instead, the phone row above becomes "back at the top", and option A or B needs a scroll or batch restore there as well.

## Options

| Option | What it does | What the reader sees | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A — page in the URL** | `ListView` takes a controlled page (`page` / `onPageChange` props, like `sort` already is). The host (`ObjectView`) binds it to a page-scoped query param with a name that does not collide (e.g. `pg`; final name chosen against `urlParams.ts`), written with `replace` so Back does not step through pages. The reset-to-1 rule clears the param. | Back, refresh, and a copied link all land on page 2. Applies to every host page that renders a list. | `domain:ui` · 1 PR (plugin-list + app-shell + tests) · no precedent measured |
| **B — page in session storage** | `ListView` (or the host) saves the page per object + view in `sessionStorage` and reads it back on mount. | Back lands on page 2 in the same tab. Refresh in the same tab does too. A copied link or a new tab starts at page 1. A stale stored page is clamped by the existing last-page guard. | `domain:ui` · 1 PR · no precedent measured |
| **C — keep the list mounted** | Nest the record route under the list route, or keep the list alive while the record page shows. | Back lands on page 2 with scroll and selection intact. | `domain:ui` · multi-PR routing change across the record-page v2 surface (#26676) · no precedent measured |
| **D — keep as is** | Document that full-page and phone opening start the list at page 1. | Unchanged: page-mode objects and every phone user lose their place. | none |

Business meaning, one line each:
- **A**: the list's address says where you are, the way a numbered page in a search result does. Back, refresh and sharing all keep it.
- **B**: the browser tab remembers where you were. The address does not, so a link you send opens on page 1.
- **C**: the list never closes behind the record. Same experience as the drawer, at a much larger routing cost.
- **D**: anyone working through a long list as full pages, or on a phone, starts over after each record.

## Four facets

<!-- os-decision-facets -->
- ① Long-term soundness: A stays inside an existing rule (page-scoped params, `urlParams.ts`) and an existing pattern (the list already takes `sort` from its host). B adds a second, invisible store for list state beside the URL. C widens the routing contract of the record page. D adds nothing.
- ② Business pull: every phone reader, and every desktop reader of an object declared `navigation.mode: 'page'` or with the reader preference `page`, hits this on any list longer than one page. Desktop drawer users do not.
- ③ AI-error resistance: A keeps the state visible in the URL, so a wrong page is plain to see. B can silently restore a stale page (bounded by the existing last-page clamp). C has the widest surface for silent regressions in record-page routing.
- ④ Startup-stage scope: A and B add no spec key and no metadata surface. C is a structural change. D is free.

Prior rulings read: pagination,pager,page-number,list-state,back-navigation → 1 hits; none; thread: not read (no --card); repo: objectstack-ai/objectstack

## Recommendation

**A.** End state in two years: the list's address carries the page, as GitHub's issue list (`?page=2`) and Jira's issue navigator (`startIndex`) already do. Back, refresh and sharing all agree, and the drawer and the full page behave the same. B is cheaper to wire but does not survive sharing, and it hides state the URL should show. C costs several times more for the same visible result. D leaves the phone experience broken.

Self-check: "Looking only at ①, choose A. Do ②③④ flip it? No."

Confidence gap: not reproduced in a running app yet, and the phone list's paging style (pager or load-more) is not measured. Both are listed under Premise.

## After a ruling

- **A**: `domain:ui` dev. Add controlled `page`/`onPageChange` to `ListView` (fall back to internal state when the host passes none, so other hosts are unchanged). Bind it in `ObjectView` to the chosen query param with `replace`. Make the reset-to-1 path clear the param. Tests: page 2 → open as full page → back shows page 2; a filter change resets to page 1 and clears the param; a too-large page in the URL clamps to the last page.
- **B**: same `ListView` seam, with a `sessionStorage` key `object:view` instead of the URL, and the same three tests.
- **C / D**: no dev dispatch until scoped (C), or close with a docs note (D).

Reader who acts: the maintainer for the ruling, then `domain:ui`.

Related: #26676 (record page v2: drawer by default, page by declaration), #27058 (phone: the record is always a page), #28915 (drawer is the default; split retired).

Dedupe (all `repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack is:issue`): `pagination page reset back list` (29, none relevant), `page number back from record` (none relevant), `list page restore` (none relevant), `serverPage` (0), `back button list loses page` (none relevant), `list state lost navigating back` (2, none relevant), `scroll position list back record` (none relevant). **New.**
